newsitem.title: UK: London's River Thames to get a new lease of life.
newsitem.headline: London's River Thames to get a new lease of life.

text.p: The River Thames will be given a new lease of life thanks to the first official planning framework for London's main artery, the British government said on Tuesday.

"The River Thames is one of the nation's major natural assets which, sadly, is often neglected or under-used. I want the river to be a focus for the capital, a living, working waterway," said Environment Secretary John Gummer.
A major aim of the Strategic Planning Guidance, which applies from Windsor to the west of London to the sea in the east, is to promote the use of the Thames as a means of transport.
"The river's potential for transporting both goods and people, and thereby removing traffic from London's congested roads is enormous."
To meet this aim the government has issued statutory directions to safeguard 32 wharves between Hammersmith in west London and Newham in east London.
The guidance will also aim to improve the built-up areas around the river and encourage use of derelict and declining areas.
Conservation and enhancement of natural and historic sites are also highlighted in the initiative.
"It's underused, undefunded and underestimated. I want it to be a working river," said the environment secretary.
"The Thames is the reason for London. There's a 1000 years of history in it."
